xibarri-uxui-case-study.title: XIBARRI - UX/UI Case Study
xibarri-uxui-case-study.desc:
Role: Founder and sole designer; Brand identity, illustration, research, user flows, wireframes and UI design.
Context: Self-initiated. It started from my own and my surroundings' experiences of missing Catalan festivals.
Status: MVP in progress
How I’ll measure success: Events saved or attended through the app, organisers publishing their own events, and returning users during festival season.
mods:
TEXT:Xibarri is a mobile application that centralizes the festivals, traditions, and cultural events of Catalonia on a single platform, facilitating access for both residents and tourists.
The app seeks to preserve and promote the rich catalan culture, offering a practical and modern tool to discover and participate in the authentic celebrations of the territory.

TEXT:Original Story:
Having recently moved to Barcelona, barely 6 months in, I was walking down Rocafort st. at around 9PM to take the metro.
I started hearing tribal percussion sounds, along with fireworks emitted from people dressed as demons. At that time, I had no idea what was going on. From my first impression, I thought it was a satanic ritual, with me terrified of possibly becoming their sacrifice victim.
A year later, I met my catalan friend who has been many years in the world of “correfocs”, and invited me to see the shows, assuring me it was nothing satanic, but only a famous Catalan tradition that dates back to the 7th century.
That moment opened a whole new world for me, with so many diverse traditional festivities of Catalonia, that I currently deeply enjoy and practice.
But I was faced with a problem; I had difficulties to find out about these festivities, because many of them were not advertised on the streets with posters, social media... but when finally I knew about them by word of mouth, the dates had already passed. From this experience, and my love of Catalan cultural festivals, the app concept was born.

oqtima-portal-uxui-design.title: OQtima App - Brand Refresh + UX/UI Case Study
oqtima-portal-uxui-design.desc:
Role: Self-initiated proposal. I did the research, user flow, persona, brand refresh and UI design on my own.
Context: In-house at OQtima, 2026. The broker had a desktop-only portal, with a picture of someone holding a phone on the main hero banner.
Status: Proposal, not built. Presented to the marketing team, who welcomed the idea.
How I’d measure success: Share of logins and trades from mobile, and fewer users switching to desktop to deposit or withdraw.
mods:
TEXT:OQtima reimagines trading as a calm, intuitive everyday experience. From market data and order execution to portfolio tracking, risk management and performance insights, everything comes together in one seamless mobile platform designed around the way traders actually work.
Purpose
For a trading platform, trust and credibility are everything; A more solid and coherent identity tells potential clients, partners, and investors that OQtima is serious, stable, and thrives to stand out from the rest.
Competitive Differentiation
A distinct visual identity and a memorable slogan can take the brand to a different level
Customer Acquisition Cost
The stronger the brand identity, the more conversion rate of client acquisition
Retention & Loyalty
Traders who feel aligned with a brand’s identity stay longer
Timing
OQtima is launching competitions, promotions, collaborating with new campaigns, and currently we are looking to build a community around the brand for social media. So it would make all the sense to refresh the brand and align it with the top competitors.

exwalt-branding.title: Exwalt - Branding
exwalt-branding.desc: EXWALT Teknoloji, Sanayi, Ticaret LTD is a tech startup whose core business is video games.
mods:
